analysis.title: Who's Next? Meet The Junk Bonds That Are One CoreWeave Away From Distress
key_insights: CoreWeave bonds traded at distressed levels for a third straight day. The 9.625% notes due 2032 closed above 80 cents on the dollar with a yield-to-worst near 14%, and the April-issued 2031s yielded above 16% (Reuters). Five-year CDS closed at a record 1,117bps, implying roughly 63% odds of default within five years.

Jensen Huang said CoreWeave's cost of capital is 'actually decreasing'. Nvidia holds a ~$2B stake in CoreWeave and helped rescue its downsized IPO. 2032 bondholders who bought at issuance in June are now at prices starting with a 7.

Morgan Stanley's HY data center tracker counts at least 20 project-finance-style bonds, $45.6B of debt backing 4,063MW of critical IT capacity across eight tenants. Each bond is issued by a special-purpose entity that owns a powered shell and is repaid from a single tenant's lease payments.

CoreWeave is the tenant on 7 of the 20 bonds: $14.1B of debt (31% of the total) financing 1,512MW (37% of capacity). It is the largest source of rent in the HY data center market, ahead of the Google-backstopped Fluidstack deals ($11.9B) and Nvidia ($8.4B).

CoreWeave-dependent issuers named: Applied Digital (APLD), Core Scientific (CORZ, $3.3B, 590MW), Galaxy Digital (GLXY, $3.51B 9.875% notes, Helios campus in Lubbock TX, final delivery March 2028), Edged ($1.3B), Elk Grove Village ($0.9B) and DDC 01 Propco ($1.12B, priced Sept 23).

As of Sept 28, the seven CoreWeave-tenant bonds averaged ~400bps spread versus ~195bps on the four Google-backstopped Fluidstack deals (Cipher, TeraWulf, Flash, Meridian) and ~150bps on Amazon-leased shells. Spread differences track the tenant's name and whether a hyperscaler co-signed.

Widest bonds in the MS table: Zenith Arc (Jane Street tenant, Oklahoma, delivery Oct 2028) 599bps / 11.09% yield, Galaxy 559bps / 10.68%, Edged 498bps / 9.92% (+160bps since issuance), SE Cosmos (SoftBank tenant) 451bps. Galaxy's 2031s were only 66bps inside CoreWeave's own 2030 unsecured notes.

Applied Digital's original 9.25% 2030s (final delivery Oct 31, 2026) traded at 104.75 and 218bps, showing that the closer a shell is to energized and paying, the less the tenant matters. CoreWeave unsecureds were at 625-808bps on Sept 28, and the 2032s fell from 85.80 to about 76 intraday.

JPMorgan cut Applied Digital's project finance bonds to Neutral from Overweight, citing a 'supply overhang', and estimates Applied Digital may need roughly $8B more secured project debt. Cipher's Google-backstopped 7.125% 2030s were still quoted near 99.875 (PitchBook).

Vintage problem: MS's loan-to-cost vs yield-to-call scatter shows 2Q26 and 3Q26 cohorts at 85-95% LTC and 13-17% yield-to-call, meaning the most recent deals have the least equity cushion and the highest required returns.

Oracle-leased bonds (Applied Digital Polaris Forge 2, Yondr Loudoun County) trade 185-220bps wide of Oracle's own unsecured debt, after the Yondr gap hit nearly 300bps in early September. Oracle CDS widened 31bps on Wednesday, and Morgan Stanley warned that data center delays could hurt Oracle's debt.

Tract's $8.4B of bonds in Storey County NV, leased to Nvidia, traded at 355-386bps on Sept 28 (+143 to +162bps since issuance). MS calls the TRACT/NVDA relationship 'now an exception' to the usual 80-240bps gap behind an IG tenant's debt, because final delivery is not until mid-2028.

SoftBank sold a record $10B of USD junk bonds in September (plus EUR1.14B) and is the tenant on the $1B SE Cosmos shell in Austin. Its 9.7%-yielding 2034s are flagged as vulnerable if OpenAI's funding chain wobbles.

Goldman's Privorotsky: credit concerns have entered the AI spending equilibrium and the market is reading them as a growth shock. GS's global neocloud basket is down 20% in five sessions (about a 1st-percentile move over ten years). He says the new equilibrium favours powered capacity and strong balance sheets over leveraged middlemen.

Credit backdrop: USD CCC spreads at 1,045bps (widest in at least three years, 100th percentile of the past year), HY yields at 8.41% (one-year high). MS says CCCs have widened 400bp this year. HY cash slipped half a point Wednesday with HY AI Datacenters underperforming.
AI-related leveraged finance issuance is ~$63B per MS, with HY issuance above $50B year-to-date. AI exposure in the HY index rose from 3% to 4% in September alone.

Deutsche Bank's Brad Zelnick reiterated Buy and a $150 target on CoreWeave ('Dislocation presenting buying opportunity'). He cites $15.5B liquidity exiting Q2, a $2.6B DDTL at SOFR+550, a $4.2B 2.875% convert, 60-65% of backlog with IG customers, and new-contract unlevered IRRs up from ~15% to ~20%+. He concedes CoreWeave will need more capital over the next 12-18 months.

The article computes a ~$35B funding gap (about $45B required capex vs ~$10B NTM operating cash flow). If half were raised at ~16%, extra interest would be about $2.8B a year, above the $2.1B loss analysts expect this year.

Privorotsky says 'My gut is we've overreacted in pockets' and that financing constraints do not invalidate the demand story, especially if rates stabilise lower. MS says high-quality HY risk-reward looks good when rates stabilize. The article notes the 10-year is above 5% and December hike odds are elevated after Wednesday's hot CPI.

The author's conclusion is to side with the bond market. Vulnerability order: the $14.1B of CoreWeave-dependent shells first (Galaxy, Core Scientific, Applied Digital, Edged), then long-dated construction stories (Zenith, Tract), then Oracle and SoftBank tenants. Life insurers, the biggest buyers of this paper, are named as the end holders at risk.

Helios 9.875% notes at 559bps are only 66bps inside CoreWeave's own unsecured notes, with final delivery not until March 2028.

crypto_views: Galaxy Digital (GLXY), Core Scientific (CORZ), Cipher and TeraWulf, crypto-miner-turned-AI-host names, are sponsors of HY data center bonds in the MS tracker. Their credit risk now depends on tenant quality (CoreWeave versus Google-backstopped Fluidstack).

trade_ideas.description: Avoid or underweight CoreWeave-tenant HY data center bonds (Galaxy, Core Scientific, Applied Digital, Edged) in favour of Amazon-leased and Google-backstopped Fluidstack deals
trade_ideas.rationale: CoreWeave-tenant bonds average ~400bps versus ~195bps and ~150bps for the better-backed groups, and the tenant is under distress pricing.
trade_ideas.risk: Strong players absorb the weak and bad news is priced in.

trade_ideas.description: Buy CoreWeave (Deutsche Bank Buy, $150 target) on dislocation
trade_ideas.rationale: Zelnick: 'we struggle to find company specific factors that justify the recent move.'
trade_ideas.risk: Additional capital need over the next 12-18 months, funding gap near $35B.

risk_factors: CoreWeave default or lease non-payment, with $14.1B of dependent project debt
Funding gap of ~$35B at ~16% cost of capital
Construction delays at long-dated shells (Galaxy to March 2028, Zenith to Oct 2028, Tract to mid-2028)
Higher-for-longer rates, 10-year above 5% and December hike odds after hot CPI
Oracle and SoftBank tenant credit risk, and OpenAI funding chain
Fine print on Google backstops that insurers are only now reading
Lease reassignment and rent-commencement protections lacking in weaker deals

tension_points.bull_case: Deutsche Bank's Zelnick sees a buying opportunity with $15.5B liquidity, 60-65% of backlog with IG customers and unlevered IRRs near 20%+. Privorotsky thinks the market 'overreacted in pockets'.
tension_points.bear_case: CoreWeave faces a ~$35B funding gap at ~16% cost of capital, and its tenant-linked bonds ($14.1B) have little protection if lease payments stop. The author takes the bond market's side.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Rates stabilizing lower (Privorotsky and MS condition), while a 10-year above 5% and December hike odds after hot CPI work against it.

tension_points.bull_case: MS says high-quality HY risk-reward looks good when rates stabilize, and the strong are expected to absorb the weak.
tension_points.bear_case: Lower-quality issuers and project-level debt are more sensitive to rates, and construction delays could drive volatility.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Rates stabilizing and deliveries completing on time. Applied Digital's near-finished shell trading at 104.75 shows the delivery effect.
